system.summary: Three different homophonic substitutions in graphic signs with nulls, syllable signs (con, et, -rum) and a few name codes (P2, P3, P4-5); P1 a letter-like sign system not identified.
system.sibling_key: none (DECODE R1853 is the c. 1401-1420 register; no 1428-30 key)
system.notes: P2: bold nabla = s, dotted nabla = null. P3: code signs for signor Malatesta, fiol del s. marchese, papa. P4-5: x written cx; et/con/-rum signs.

prior_solution.where: P3 only: contemporary interlinear decipherment on the letter. DECODE status 'Partially decrypted' with no transcription.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE login cookie and /goal target setting. No target-specific intervention.
tools: r1854/solve.py homophonic annealer on lang/ models

solution.what: Fetched R1854 (5 images), the R1853 register (14 images) and DECODE metadata with the saved cookie.

Viewed the images: four letters to Gianfrancesco Gonzaga (Rome 22 Apr and 9 Aug 1428, Forli 6 Nov 1428, Rome 13/21 Feb 1430), not one; P3 carries an interlinear decipherment; P5 is an upside-down verso.
Web search for Pandolfo Malatesta's ciphered letters (Treccani DBI; Falcioni 2015 prints the plaintext of his 1438 cipher letter, ASMn AG b. 1081).
Read the R1853 register keys (Malatesta keys on f. 1, 1406-1419 keys): none match the 1428-30 letters.
First-pass sign transcription of P2 (37 lines) by the model.
P2: IC 0.040, 46 sign types -> homophonic; the triangle precedes sign 17 in 21 of 29 cases -> q/u.
Homophonic anneal on P2 with the Latin model and q/u fixed: Latin words appear (quod, predicto, ibidem, filium).
P2 second pass at 5x separating look-alike glyphs.
Per-sign and per-occurrence rescoring of P2 finds nulls, the bold/dotted nabla split (s/null) and con/et/rum signs; P2 reads as continuous Latin.
First-pass transcription of P4 (28 lines) and P5 (3 lines).
Latin anneal on P4 gives readable Latin (post recessum, sollicitabo bullam, galeotam); key applied to P5.
Subagent second pass of P4 and P5 against the image with the key: 209 edits, glyph splits.
P4 and P5 read in full apart from four short spots.
Subagent read P3's faint interlinear gloss (about two-thirds legible) and the three name codes.
Subagent transcribed P3's 894 cipher signs with gloss letters attached.
P3 key from the gloss (30 sign values) plus rare signs from context; whole letter deciphered from the signs.
P1 cipher runs transcribed (266 signs).
P1 anneals in Latin and Italian, with and without spaces, costed nulls, vowel constraint, reversed orders, split and merged digraphs: no reading.
Solver reads a synthetic 266-letter monoalphabetic Latin text, also with 12% token noise: P1 is not a simple substitution in Latin.
Register key 'cum Malatesta dni Pandulfi' values seeded into the P1 anneal: -4.2/char, no fit.
Opened all other Mantova records on DECODE (R7858-R7888): 16th-17th century keys.
Subagent second pass of P1 (262 signs, 3 runs, 3 misreadings fixed) and clear-text transcription.
P1 re-solved from the second pass in Latin, Italian and modern Italian: no reading.

outcome.fraction_read_source: Cipher signs read as sense per letter: P2 1740/1802, P3 869/894, P4 1486/1537, P5 199/199, P1 0/262 -> 4294/4694 = 0.915 (tokens measured with _check_profile.py on ct_p*.txt; doubtful spans hand-counted in reading_p2/p3/p4.md).
outcome.notes: Three of the four letters read (P2, P3, P4+P5). P1, Pandolfo Malatesta's 22 April 1428 runs, not read: an unidentified system, no key.

gaps.detail: not a simple or homophonic substitution; register keys do not fit; key material likely ASMn AG b. 1081 c. 159-160 (1438 cipher letter) with b. 840 c. 95 (its translation), not online

gaps.item: P2 code ARO and doubtful spans
